English: Earthen Storehouse
A simple pit or earthen mound, hastily dug to safeguard tithes and offerings, providing modest security and spiritual assurance against famine.
Wooden Granary
A timber-framed granary, raised above the ground to shield sacred grain from pests, supporting the temples stores and attracting the faithful in times of scarcity.
Stone Granary
Solid stone walls defend the temples bounty from thieves and vermin alike, symbolizing divine protection of the communitys sustenance.
Grain Drying Shed
A covered, ventilated structure for drying and preserving grains, maximizing tithes and sustaining the temple through lean years.
Guarded Granary
An imposing store protected by temple guards and sturdy doors, this granary is both a symbol of faith and a bastion of plenty in troubled times.
Multi-Level Granary
A tall, layered granary with multiple stories, allowing for vast stores and improved organization of sacred offerings, further bolstering the temples wealth and defense.
Granary Loft
A lofted granary with complex timberwork and improved storage, ensuring offerings remain dry, secure, and available for the needy. Requires improved construction techniques.
Secured Storehouse
A granary reinforced with iron fittings and guarded by temple stewards, deterring theft and ensuring the temples influence during hardship.
Granary Tower
A fortified granary tower serves as both granary and watchpost, protecting the temples stores from raiders and showing the community the strength of faith.
Sanctuary Granary Complex
A sprawling, sanctified complex of interconnected granaries, chapels, and fortified halls, a beacon of spiritual security and prosperity in the land.
